## Single-paint opacity investigation (2026-10-07)

This is an isolated Windows experiment against production `2204ab1b`, not a
renderer repair. Production counts and the validated delivery checkpoint above
remain unchanged. Thirty-two authored CC0 sources / 96 configurations were
declared before prototype edits or browser capture/comparison. They vary direct
versus group opacity, two opacity values, three backgrounds, rounded/straight/path
fills, gradients, translucent fills, fill/stroke and disjoint/overlapping children.
All 288 retained fresh-process captures are byte-stable, healthy and cleaned.
Four failed attempt sets remain separate; their complete triples were retried
sequentially rather than accepting PNGs from timed-out invocations.

The pinned Chromium [playback iterator](https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/153.0.8010.52/cc/paint/paint_op_buffer_iterator.cc)
folds a SaveLayerAlpha/drawing-op/Restore sequence only when the nested record
contains one eligible paint operation. Text blobs and multiple-operation records
retain the layer. [Raster flags](https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/153.0.8010.52/cc/paint/scoped_raster_flags.h)
multiply float alpha. This is native paint-operation provenance, not SVG child
count or managed geometry count: one stroke can lower into several geometries,
and one managed rectangle can contain both fill and stroke paints. State operations
inside a record can also prevent folding.

Production renders 45 configurations exactly and 45 with differences, rejecting
six direct filled/stroked rounded rectangles with element opacity. Browser twins
confirm identical direct/group images for the six single-element shape families,
including fill/stroke; the two multiple-child families have distinct outputs.
The diagnostic immediate-single-geometry byte-fold model produces 66 exact,
24 differing and six rejected configurations. It closes 21 controls and five old
research configurations, preserves every other complete report/PNG in the
1,558-case bank and every corporate report/PNG in the 258-variant matrix, but
worsens all three translucent-fill controls at opacity 0.4375. These are model
results, not fixture graduations or platform delivery evidence.

For example, independently rounding fill opacity 0.7 and group opacity 0.4375
gives byte factors 179 and 112, whose round/255 product is 79. Multiplying the
source floats before solid-color packing gives 78. The pinned [Blink paint resolver](https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/153.0.8010.52/third_party/blink/renderer/core/paint/svg_object_painter.cc)
retains solid-color alpha as float while quantizing paint-server fill/stroke opacity
before layer folding. [Skia solid packing](https://skia.googlesource.com/skia/+/f8b66b7597c4cc859d3ed190e9c6872241e6721c/src/core/SkSwizzlePriv.h)
uses the final float value. The next repair must retain these distinct precision
boundaries, logical operation identity and complete multiple-paint element effects,
with bounded copying, ownership and resource checks. A physical geometry shortcut
does not establish the required semantics. Full experimental evidence stays under
ignored `artifacts/opacity-folding-20261007/`; no implementation fingerprints or
new tracked corpus entries are introduced by this investigation.

The preceding white-mask-copy probe uses `fill-opacity="0.7"`, not element opacity.
Its residual belongs to paint-alpha/coverage and copy composition; the earlier
checkpoint descriptions have been corrected accordingly.

The model assigns logical identities before lowering, preserves them across

### Owned paint values, recording scopes and inspector replay

Twelve further authored CC0 controls were declared after the earlier model
comparison, before their own edits or capture/comparison. All 36 fresh-process
captures are byte-stable, healthy and cleaned. They move transforms and clips
between parents and leaves, copy source opacity through zero/translated instances,
nest parent/source opacity, and cover translucent strokes, near-opaque gradients,
root opacity and a white mask. Production has eight exact and four differing
results. The earlier global foldability flag has four exact and eight differing
results, including five regressions of previously exact controls. An old-bank
comparison alone therefore did not establish recording-state parity.

The revised isolated model gives each logical paint and opacity command a typed
recording scope. Local clip/transform state outside a leaf's own opacity stays
distinct from state inside its parent's opacity; mask and root viewport state
retain their separate barriers. Instance mapping copies scope values through
bounded parser-owned caches. It reaches **10/12 exact**, with one differing pixel
in each transformed control, preserves the earlier **126/144** and four exact
state twins, and retains the explicit line-fill rejection. All eight production
exact results in the new set remain exact.

The first scoped attempt regressed three full-canvas fixtures by sixteen pixels
each because the fast path still read geometry alpha instead of the owned paint
value; that consumer now reads the retained value. Early collapse of source
opacity separately regressed the nested parent/source zero-position instance by
462 pixels and was removed. The pinned
[playback iterator](https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/153.0.8010.52/cc/paint/paint_op_buffer_iterator.cc)
decides whether to fold a parent before replaying its nested record; an inner
opacity operation can prevent that fold. Preserve the nested effects until this
decision, then fold the eligible inner paint during playback.

Inspector snapshots cannot justify removing those nested effects. The pinned
[PictureLayer implementation](https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/153.0.8010.52/cc/layers/picture_layer.cc)
rasters the display list into a SkPictureRecorder. The inspector
[PictureSnapshot implementation](https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/153.0.8010.52/third_party/blink/renderer/platform/graphics/picture_snapshot.cc)
then logs or replays that picture. Re-recording may simplify operations. Three
fresh, healthy, cleaned snapshot/replay probes keep actual screenshot bytes
identical to the frozen controls. The single-source and root-opacity picture
replays match those screenshots, but the nested parent/source replay differs by
**462 pixels**, maximum channel error 34 and maximum alpha error one. Its complete
mismatch tuple equals the rejected early-collapse model. The derived picture
shows no opacity layer even though its pixels differ from actual page rendering.
This proves a limitation of the inspector evidence; it does not identify every
original browser operation. Actual browser screenshots remain the fidelity oracle.

Paint values now belong to a reserved scene arena. Geometries retain two four-byte
handles; commands retain source opacity without growing their layout. Geometry

## Direct paint outside path row storage (2026-10-08)

The retained scaled masked circle exposed a direct paint emitted just outside its

path storage, while direct real-blitter operations retain the destination clip.
Fixed-edge conic advancement can emit a fringe beyond the original path interval.
The managed event index and output traversal had discarded that direct paint.

Direct events now retain the bitmap/SVG clip. Their links grow only when an actual
emission escapes existing storage, with bounded geometric capacity growth and an
offset for either side. Pending mask/run coverage keeps its original row width;
classification and curve construction stay unchanged. All four polygon paint
consumers extend each row's destination interval only to emitted fringe paints,
intersect it with the exclusive CPU interior and charge the additional pixels.
Unused link capacity does not expand output traversal.

Growth charges initialization and copying before allocation, reserves old and new
arrays together, checks cancellation during bounded copying and releases owners
after success or failure. Reused extra link capacity is charged when cleared on
later rows. Four core cases protect emitted paint beyond an unchanged pending
row, cancellation at growth and replay, and denial while both arrays are live.
No fixed pixel margin, per-image predicate or reference adjustment is introduced.

## SVG rounded-rectangle command order (2026-10-08)

The rounded hairline had exact alpha coverage but three differing color pixels.
Native browser recordings show SVG paths starting at the top tangent, followed
by the top edge and clockwise corners. Simplified ovals start at the top midpoint.

or its simplified oval index three. This preserved the same geometric contour

## Ordered symbol children and native instance replay (2026-10-08)

Each child had previously been registered under its containing symbol ID, so
valid multiple-child symbols failed as duplicate IDs. A bounded builder now
owns ordered child definitions until one complete symbol transfers to the
registry. Child IDs borrow geometry owners; symbol wrapping copies geometry
slots when necessary so aliases exclude container opacity/viewBox. Failure
disposes unregistered children, while registry cleanup skips borrowed aliases.
All child, binding and instance-array growth/copies reserve storage and charge
work before allocation. A newly mapped geometry retains a guard until list
insertion succeeds; exhaustive denial caught and closed the earlier gap between
native mapping and denied list growth.

Per-channel fill bindings distinguish inherited fill from authored child/symbol
fill and from stroke. Instance fill changes only the inherited channels; opacity
and color retain their own inheritance. Container styles use the shared cascade,
and child/symbol/use opacity retain separate recording scopes. The admitted
subset follows [SVG 1.1 use inheritance](https://www.w3.org/TR/SVG11/struct.html#UseElement):
authored properties belong to the referenced content and inherited properties
come from use and its ancestors. Tested child aliases exclude the enclosing
symbol's fill and opacity; alias stroke inheritance remains an explicit gap.

Magnification no longer rejects geometry that retains original curve commands.
It replays those commands through the existing final map rather than scaling
lowering-time subdivision error. Circle/ellipse definition fills retain original
float oval conics too, closing omitted-viewport magnification. Fallback flattened
content without an authored tape and existing non-uniform/consumer gates remain.
No observed document coordinates, identifiers or failure pixels select behavior.

clipping differences are repaired in the [viewport-opacity follow-up](#isolated-opacity-under-symbol-viewport-clips-2026-10-08) below.

Nested symbol groups and local uses retain ordered typed source nodes rather
than XML or an eagerly transformed scene. The direct-leaf route stays available.
Entering the content route migrates existing leaf owners only after successful
append; group/use/leaf aliases borrow their own range or geometry. Sealing reserves
the source array before allocation, releases construction storage on success,
and preserves owners after work denial or cancellation so assembly can retry.

An iterative validator checks local references, including unused/anonymous
definitions. Circular dependencies are MalformedInput; undefined local targets
remain UnsupportedFeature. The expander uses budgeted frames and the existing
instance geometry/paint mapping. Each clone composes source-order transforms,
independent solid-fill inheritance, display/visibility and opacity scopes.
Repeated acyclic references remain separate paints. Empty forward targets keep
a typed non-painting placeholder so later scene commands remain valid.
Partial forward insertion now disposes every unadopted native owner and reserves
extra command storage before allocation; two new ownership sweeps exposed that
cleanup gap. Six new exhaustive sweeps and eighteen graph, depth, expansion,
sealing/retry, empty-target and discovery checks cover the slice.

All three retained nested-content rejections graduate to exact results without
source/reference changes. [Sixteen new controls](../tests/Research/symbol-content/manifest.json)
give fifteen exact results and one measured difference. In `group-alias-use`,
a fractional symbol viewport intersects a translucent group: 123 pixels differ,
including 21 alpha pixels, maximum channel/alpha error 30. [Three diagnostic
twins](../tests/Research/symbol-content-diagnostics/manifest.json) retain the same
difference in the equivalent inline group, while opaque and unclipped forms
are exact. This isolates a clipping/opacity interaction; its full mechanism
remains unproved. No alias-specific pixel rule is justified.

A trial that deferred the viewport clip to group composition did not match:
137 pixels differed, 14 alpha pixels, maximum alpha error 16 and maximum channel
error 255. It was discarded. The unchanged originals, stable healthy browser
capture triples and measured differences remain visible for the next G5 repair.
Every one of the 65 symbol comparisons runs through all six outputs: 63 exact
and two known differences. These controls stay outside the original bank and
corporate denominators. Raster fields/surfaces, public APIs and dependencies
are unchanged; no quantitative performance claim is made. Detailed results
remain ignored under `artifacts/symbol-content-20261008/` and isolated Linux
`symbol-content-final-20261008/`.

## Isolated opacity under symbol viewport clips (2026-10-08)

The retained alias and equivalent inline group each differed at 123 pixels,
including 21 alpha pixels, under a fractional symbol viewport and opacity.
Their opaque and unclipped twins were exact. Clipping each child before
isolation repeated viewport coverage; restoring a clipped layer through the
existing direct image blitter still used the wrong opacity/coverage order.

At the pinned Skia revision, `SkDraw.cpp::clipHandlesSprite` accepts a BW clip
or an image wholly within opaque AA runs. Otherwise `drawSprite` uses an
unfiltered image shader: `SkBitmapProcState.cpp` scales premultiplied lanes by
paint opacity before `SkBlitter_ARGB32.cpp` applies the AA run through the native
row blend. The managed restore now follows that dispatch and arithmetic.
Inherited viewport clips wrap isolated symbol groups; children retain their
local clips. Viewport allocation bounds round outward, while existing mask
regions keep their separate hard-edge policy. Source path ink bounds enclose
in source coordinates before the device map, preserving the isolated bitmap
origin. The region discriminator occupies existing command padding; draw commands
remain 72 bytes, geometry 272 bytes and recorded paint values 68 bytes.

[Eighteen predeclared controls](../tests/Research/symbol-viewport-opacity/manifest.json)
cover right/bottom and left/top crossings, integral placement, nested scopes,
different paints and translucent content on transparent, white and black
backgrounds. Three healthy fresh-process captures per case are stable and cleaned.
The preceding renderer matched only three controls. The shader-order repair
initially left three nested-scope cases with a one-byte color error at one pixel;
rounding source bounds before mapping removes it. All eighteen controls and both
retained residuals now match unchanged references through all six outputs.
The earlier clip-placement-only trial remains rejected; the missing shader
dispatch and source-bound order explain why placement alone was insufficient.

Windows and isolated Linux Release builds have zero warnings/errors and 4,444
passing tests each (3,981 core, 457 visual-project, six FontProbe). All 83 symbol
comparisons are exact. Three additional exhaustive work/memory sweeps protect
retained viewport/group metadata; focused tests distinguish viewport restoration from
mask allocation regions. Clip setup charges bounded work; cleanup preserves
the existing cancellation and ownership contracts. Public APIs, dependencies
and surface count are unchanged; no quantitative performance claim is made.
All 1,567 original reports and 1,545 PNG bytes remain unchanged from the preceding
retained-content checkpoint. Corporate results remain 27/27 documents and
258/258 variants exact against each platform's own references; every corporate
report/PNG is unchanged. Ignored evidence lives under
`artifacts/symbol-viewport-opacity-20261008/` and isolated Linux
`symbol-viewport-opacity-final-20261008/`. Remaining inherited stroke/paint and
use styling stay G2; wider viewport, clip and mask combinations stay G5.

## Use paint properties and source stroke identity (2026-10-08)

The local-use attribute policy and presentation resolver now admit solid `color`
and `fill-opacity` together. Source paint properties remain independently authored
or inherited, following [SVG use inheritance](https://www.w3.org/TR/SVG2/struct.html#UseStyleInheritance).
Nested retained uses resolve their own typed style against the current instance
context rather than replacing their authored color/opacity with the parent values.
Ordinary definitions reuse their retained source bindings, so authored fills win
over use fills and line strokes ignore use fill. Four former rejection assertions
now verify that source precedence instead of preserving erroneous admission gates.

Source recording retains fill/stroke identity after lowering markers disappear.
The tag sits beside the existing Boolean in recorded paint, preserving its 68-byte
size; geometry remains 272 bytes and commands 72 bytes. CurrentColor strokes bind
against source/instance color with their independent stroke opacity. Fill opacity
does not dim that channel. Native recoloring and mapped paint alpha use the same
resolved source binding. Binding arrays reserve their actual expanded element size;
six new exhaustive ownership sweeps cover success, partial expansion and two
retained rejection cases. Malformed numeric use paint values release parser owners.

[Thirty-one retained controls](../tests/Research/use-paint-properties/manifest.json)
give twenty exact comparisons, six measured stroke differences and five explicit
rejections through all six outputs. The main 27 cases were declared before editing
and browser comparison; four supplemental diagnostics were declared after the first
prototype to distinguish raster/admission boundaries. All 93 accepted captures are
stable healthy fresh-process triples with cleaned profiles. Eighteen preceding
color/fill-opacity rejections become exact. The existing simple symbol paint-server
anchor and the native inline twin remain exact. Paint-server use fill opacity,
inherited shader-definition opacity, inherited symbol stroke, rendered-group use
paint and transformed inline rectangle strokes retain explicit gates.

The native-stroke symbol family differs at two pixels on each background; transparent
output has maximum channel error 10 and no alpha error. Its native inline twin is
exact under both the preceding and current renderer. Fractional instanced rectangle
strokes differ at 85/81/85 pixels; transparent output has 46 alpha differences and
maximum channel/alpha error 19. Chrome's retained trace draws a stroked frame, while
the renderer paints four rectangle bands. The pinned `SkScan_Antihair.cpp::AntiFrameRect`
keeps outer hull, frame and inverse-biased inner fringe operations separate; the
current seam/corner model still needs repair. The inline rectangle twin hits its
separate transform/paint gate. Sources, references and all measured differences
stay frozen for the next G4/G5 fidelity work; source retention alone is not exactness.

A contained-path clip-classification trial was discarded: the native symbol family

containment alone does not justify changing that routing. This is negative evidence,

## Ordered rectangle stroke frames (2026-10-08)

The three retained currentColor rectangle-stroke comparisons now match their
unchanged browser references. Previously they differed at 85/81/85 pixels; the
transparent comparison had 46 alpha differences and maximum channel/alpha error
19. The browser trace emits a stroked rectangle, while the previous renderer
painted four separately antialiased fractional bands. Their corners and seams
had different coverage and repeated source-over arithmetic.

`SvgRectangleFrameCoverage` adapts the pinned `SkScan_Antihair.cpp::AntiFrameRect`:
truncate mapped float edges to 24.8, align subpixel thin hulls, paint the outer
hull, fill the integer middle frame, then emit the inverse inner fringe with
rounded inverse-alpha union. Each pixel retains up to four operations in source
order, including two coincident inner edges. A collapsed inner box becomes a
filled middle. Solid strokes over solid, linear/radial and pattern fills share
this route; fill painting remains independent.

The immutable frame owns no storage and borrows only a four-byte stack span per
call. The converter charges setup, both row passes and coverage/operation visits
before painting; empty interiors are skipped. Cancellation is checked during
setup and each row of both passes. Three work-denial checks cover narrow, wide
and collapsed frames and confirm that surface owners release. Draw commands,
geometry and recorded paint remain 72/272/68 bytes, with no added surfaces,
public APIs or dependencies and no quantitative performance claim.

[Fifteen independent controls](../tests/Research/rectangle-frames/manifest.json)
were declared after the first frame prototype and before their captures or
comparisons. Forty-five healthy, cleaned fresh-process captures form stable
triples. Twelve prior render differences become exact through six outputs:
fractional frames, root-scaled subpixel strokes, collapsed inner boxes and
shader-fill frames, each on transparent/white/black backgrounds. Three explicit
clip-crossing cases retain the viewport-boundary admission gate. The earlier
transformed inline rectangle twin retains its separate gate; frame fidelity does
not establish those combinations as supported.

The 31-case use-paint bank is now 23 exact, three native symbol stroke differences
and five unsupported outcomes. The native stroke family still differs at two
pixels per background; the inline twin remains exact. Parsed source/instance
colors and independent alphas agree, leaving the clip/raster routing to diagnose.
The discarded whole-path-contained clip classification remains negative evidence;
no such routing change is part of this repair.

## Native closed rectangle path strokes (2026-10-08)

The three retained currentColor native symbol stroke backgrounds now match their
unchanged browser references; their inline twin stays exact. The preceding two-pixel
residual had no alpha error and maximum channel error 10 on transparent output.
Paint binding was correct. The generic outline retained redundant inner join lines,
which split the affected row into quarter/half/quarter strips. The forced AA/RLE
route accumulated coverage 64, while the native rectangle ring yielded 63. Changing
clip classification was the wrong model; the earlier containment trial remains
discarded evidence and AA clip dispatch is unchanged.

The pinned `SkStroke::strokePath` recognizes explicitly closed rectangular paths
before entering `SkPathStroker`. `SvgRectanglePathRecognizer` now shares the existing
`SkPathPriv::IsRectContour` adaptation between filled-path coverage and source stroke
construction. It retains float bounds, direction and explicit closure, including
zero lines and monotone collinear segments. Each caller maps and charges original
verbs under its own cancellation/work contract. Open rectangle paths, curves and
multiple contours continue through generic joins/caps. Non-scaling construction
maps before recognition; ordinary final scene/instance placement stays separate.

The rectangle route follows `SkStroke::strokeRect`: sorted/outset float bounds,
miter below sqrt(2) becoming bevel, eight-point bevel corners, native round corners
with quarter-circle conics and legacy starting points, and an opposite inner rectangle
only when the stroke width fits both dimensions. Round radius normalization and
oval/square degeneration preserve the pinned raw-shape conventions. The immutable
result and mutable pass state own no storage; outline scratch is bounded on the stack
and output growth uses the existing reserved parser list. No generic stroker private
lists, extra surfaces, public API or dependency are added. Every admitted work/memory
denial is swept for each join; cancellation/retry and four construction maps pass.

A new native oracle retains 480 outlines from unchanged compiled `strokeRect`,
`addBevel`, raw rectangle/rounded-rectangle constructors and `SkRRect` normalization,
through a record sink. Both directions, every join, cutoff and very wide strokes
match all float bits. The preceding 1,920 direct-verb generic stroker goldens remain
unchanged and are exercised by the explicitly named `BuildGeneric` entry; their
metadata already excludes rectangle specialization. Production uses full dispatch.

[Thirty controls](../tests/Research/rectangle-path-strokes/manifest.json) were declared

### SVG Translate: bounded implicit quadratic scans

The shared Windows scan correction now resolves the finite curve controls from
the preceding checkpoint. All five outlines match all 150 complete translated
native RGB textures, including zero bytes and an outside margin. The two split
forms remain exact; both unsplit forms and S32 become exact. The unchanged
integer-strike SVG control consequently matches through six raw and six prepared

with maximum channel error 11; Linux stays exact. Twenty-six document pixels and

changed in either output. The browser references, source bytes, font program and
output contracts remain frozen.

The correction evaluates a quadratic's implicit equation with bounded coefficient
precision. Relative to the start, write its coordinates as
`x(t) = Bx*t + Ax*t*t`, `y(t) = By*t + Ay*t*t`. Eliminating `t` gives
`(Ay*x - Ax*y)^2 + D*(By*x - Bx*y) = 0`, where
`D = Ay*Bx - Ax*By`. Both directions are normalized, with upward font Y. The bit
widths of the determinant and maximum span determine the reduction of F26
precision: `max(0, (determinantBits + spanBits - 27) / 3)`. Relative controls,
endpoints and initial sample offsets round at that reduced precision. Initial
half-polynomial products round separately; their mixed term occurs once. First
and second differences then define the scan equation at subsequent centers.
Solving that equation supplies crossings to the existing directed winding and
smart-dropout machinery, with no per-cell curve walk or new owned storage.

This explains the independent split/unsplit controls. Exact subdivision lowers
coefficient magnitudes and therefore preserves more precision, despite unchanged
continuous geometry. A geometric tolerance, inward epsilon or rounded square root
cannot express that distinction. The independently inverted LCD cell maps also
match direct aliased native rendering under a six by five transform for all five
retained outlines and both grid-fit modes. Native input observations preserve the
original complete textures and confirm the integer scan coordinates. Diagnostic
tools and native observations remain private; the managed renderer computes the
equation from caller-owned contours.

Implied points retain half F26 units through fitting and positioning. Rounding
happens after the six by five map, where a half unit rounds upward in font Y.
Rounding the original midpoint instead changes the outline too early. This
separate stage resolves S32's third bottom-row cell while preserving its previously
correct near-center cells. Inserting explicit integer on-curve points at the
existing integer implied midpoints leaves the complete native S32 texture
unchanged, confirming that this correction needs the shared quadratic geometry
rather than a separate implementation for off-curve point groups.

The qualified implicit equation currently covers quadratics monotonic in both
axes with spans up to 50 fine-grid cells. Other curves retain their established
analytic crossings. Every additional curve evaluation consumes work and observes
cancellation; caller-owned crossing scratch and its reservation are unchanged.
The expanded regression fact protects all 150 retained textures on both platforms.
The SVG bank also asserts the newly exact integer control through all 12 APIs.
The remaining small edge details and closing-parenthesis strike determine the
next shared correction. Extend subdivision or boundary/dropout behavior when
those retained failures require it; this checkpoint closes neither the whole
document nor the finite G2–G9 and S17 exits.

## Composition sheet through shared viewport, clip and mask replay (2026-10-15)

The unchanged [composition sheet](../tests/Research/composition-sheet/README.md)
is **1/1 complete document / 4/4 exact controls** on Windows/Linux. The original
percentage-use, opposite-winding and overlapping-path controls remain in their
existing banks; the original partial-mask core input has its own MIT visual.
Inputs/options and 21 healthy stable new captures were frozen at `005b4876`
before implementation. Original Windows references were reused; missing Linux
triples were acquired once. All corresponding platform PNG bytes agree.

Ordinary/group uses carry live viewport length bases independently of use
width/height. Symbols establish a viewport from their viewBox or instance size.
Percentage oval sources bind during bounded instance lowering, including repeated
uses under different viewports; geometry and paint share the same source replay.

Retain a first rectangular path's source until sibling content is known, then
preserve the single-rectangle fast path if no sibling requires promotion.
The existing bounded convex straight child combiner normalizes winding and uses
nonzero replay for overlapping children; disjoint contours keep qualified parity,
cyclic starts and ordering. Native contour masks compose the enclosing viewport
map before replay. This is not general curved/compound sibling path union;
heterogeneous children and larger multi-shape fallback remain required G5 work.

Partial uniform instance masks reuse the same retained spatial source replay as
ordinary leaves/groups. Scalar coverage is checked in the target frame against
visual extents; default object-box regions use object bounds. Strokes, mask
source placement and element opacity retain their separate ordering. Existing
spatial instance masks no longer require full coverage where mapped replay exists.

Original rejection inputs graduate to positive regressions without deleting their
semantics. Tests cover forward/backward references, winding independence, live
percentage rebinding, meaningful allocation/work denial, active cancellation,
cleanup and exact retry. The [receipt](../artifacts/maintenance-review-20261012/composition-qualified-results.json)
owns finished qualification. This supersedes earlier percentage-instance,
overlapping-convex-child and partial-use-mask gates only; finite G2–G9/S17 remain open.
